Belfast Live: Number 1 For News And Sport Handicap

runners_data.name: Teologia
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good recently and carries the prominent/front-runner role here; Joseph O'Brien sends her in form (LR 22d) and her soft-going record is acceptable, but the step up in trip to 1m2½f on a soft surface is a query — J M Sheridan takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Hassaniya
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly with recent placed efforts at shorter trips; soft-going form at 7f suggests she handles cut, but this 1m2½f trip is an unknown and she steps up considerably in distance from her last two runs over 8f.

runners_data.name: Dreoilin
runners_data.note: Bolger-trained three-year-old with a solid soft-going record (2 places from 5 starts on similar ground); the 12f run at Goodwood suggests she stays, and two recent placed efforts over 10f on soft make her a reliable each-way profile in this shape.

runners_data.name: Amrum
runners_data.note: Hold-up style filly who scored over 10f on good and has soft-going experience; Nicola Burns claims 5lb and the tongue-tie is noted — her last win was recent (LR 19d) but she has limited experience on genuinely soft ground and maps to the rear of this field.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good and has a placed effort on soft over 8f; Scott McCullagh partners her for Mrs John Harrington and she carries the tongue-tie — her course form and recently active campaign (LR 16d) give her a live chance tracking the pace.

runners_data.name: Aquilla Star
runners_data.note: Long absence (LR 236d) is the glaring concern for this two-year-old making a seasonal return; hold-up style mapped to midfield, has a placed effort over 7f on heavy-ground adjacent conditions, but the layoff and age profile make her very hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Espritroyale
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll takes the mount for Gavin Cromwell (8 from 47 over 14 days); hold-up style with very limited soft-going form (1 from 5 on sim-going), and all recent form is at shorter trips — the step up to 1m2½f on soft is a significant negative.

runners_data.name: Roaming Coyote
runners_data.note: Placed over 10f on good for W J Lee; prominent style suits this race shape and his soft-going profile is limited but his recent trip profile is right — the trainer's modest 14-day record (1/11) is a mild concern but the style is well-placed.

runners_data.name: The Holy Apostle
runners_data.note: Modest form figures throughout and no wins recorded; placed over 8f on soft but has been well beaten on most starts — Luke McAteer rides for a trainer without a recent win (T14: 0/2) and this horse carries no compelling tactical angle.

runners_data.name: Chapel Island
runners_data.note: Consistent soft-going fader whose form figures (8, 7, 8, 12, 6) indicate a horse that struggles to land a blow; naturally a hold-up type pushed forward in the map representation — the fade-in-finish flag and style-fit discount (0.90) reflect genuine concern about its ability to matter here regardless of position.

runners_data.name: Connecteo
runners_data.note: Placed over 12f on good as his best effort; a true hold-up type carried into a midfield map position given the volume of closers in this race — the fade-in-finish flag and style-fit score (0.92) are honest warnings, and his limited soft-going form (1 from 4) adds further doubt.

runners_data.name: Arizona Star
runners_data.note: Third over 10f at the Curragh on heavy-adjacent ground is his best result; another genuine hold-up horse whose true position will be towards the rear — the style-fit discount (0.90), fade flag, and trainer with zero runners in the last 14 days combine to make him a long-shot at best.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Multiple poor efforts including three last-place finishes; Noel Meade sends him out fresh (LR 15d) with a 2/20 14-day record, but the form figures (0, 0, 0, 6, 7) speak plainly — a natural closer who will trail the field and whose chance relies on a fast-run race that looks unlikely.

races.paceDynamic: Teologia is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to contest the lead, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on soft ground over 1m2½f at Down Royal. The prominent types — Hassaniya, Dreoilin, Glamazon, and Roaming Coyote — will track just off the pace and create a compact early order, but none appears inclined to send Teologia into a fight for the lead. On soft going over this trip, a controlled lead that avoids a punishing early tempo is a significant advantage, and horses who can travel smoothly just behind the pace-setter are best positioned to pounce — meaning prominent-to-midfield runners with proven soft-ground form are favoured. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can honestly place at the rear — Chapel Island, Connecteo, Arizona Star, and Captain Con are all true closers who are redistributed to midfield on the map; in practice they will be at the back of the field where their ability to land a late blow depends entirely on the pace being strong enough to string the field out, which looks unlikely given Teologia's uncontested control.

scenarios.body: If the pace is truly dawdling and Teologia's prominent rivals fail to close the gap quickly enough in the home straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinds, Midfield Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground degrades quickly into a gruelling stamina test and the race becomes a one-paced slog from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If the soft ground degrades quickly into a gruelling stamina test and the race becomes a one-paced slog from the home turn.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly strong gallop is set and the field strings out, giving the redistributed hold-up horses a genuine target to run at.
scenarios.body: If an unexpectedly strong gallop is set and the field strings out, giving the redistributed hold-up horses a genuine target to run at.

watchPoints.text: Teologia's early lead is the race-shaping factor — watch whether any of Hassaniya, Glamazon or Roaming Coyote push up to challenge her before the home turn, which would dramatically change the pace scenario.

Amrum and Aquilla Star are both mapped as hold-up types but Amrum's tongue-tie and Aquilla Star's 236-day absence mean both could behave unpredictably in the early stages and disrupt the expected order.

Chapel Island, Connecteo, Arizona Star and Captain Con all carry fade-in-finish flags and style-fit discounts — if any of these horses is given an aggressive ride against their natural style, it could artificially inflate early pace and compromise Teologia's control.

Dreoilin's soft-going placed record (2 from 5 on similar ground) is the most reliable form line in this race on going — watch whether Declan McDonogh positions her prominently off Teologia or drops her in to get cover.

The going is soft across all races at Down Royal today with no reported deterioration — conditions should remain consistent, meaning soft-ground specialists throughout the card have a genuine advantage rather than a worsening surface to navigate.

races.name: Mongey Communications Handicap

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won over 10f at Stafford Castle and will lead here uncontested; soft going form reads 2/15 suggesting the surface is a mild query, and at OR=60 this is the class ceiling of the race but the solo-pace role may suit if fractions stay honest.

runners_data.name: Slaney Swagger
runners_data.note: Returns after 192 days off for a trainer in strong form (T14: 3/4), which is the primary angle here; has placed over today's trip and handles varying ground, though the long absence demands scrutiny and a hold-up style means traffic is possible from the rear in a big field.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose natural style fits this pace perfectly — settles just off Rising Sky and gets a clean run; won over 16f on good ground and has a placed effort over 8f, so the 10f trip on soft suits a horse that stays well and Chris Hayes is a strong booking.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: True hold-up operator whose form over 12-16f on soft is the relevant angle, but has faded in finishes and recorded 0W0P in similar going; the reality is this horse will be further forward than preferred in a race where the rear is congested, and five runs without a win including a 7th in soft at Leopardstown tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Simpson's Paradox
runners_data.note: Has run over today's 16f trip on soft ground (unplaced) and handles stamina tests, but a genuine deep closer now operating further forward than ideal in this large field; no wins or places in similar going (0W0P) and the 5-runner apprentice jockey partnership has limited race-reading experience for a 17-runner scramble.

runners_data.name: Albatala
runners_data.note: Placed runner over 17f on good ground twice and handles an extreme stamina test, but 1m2½f may be sharp for a horse who has gone 18f-20f in recent starts; another true hold-up type displaced from its preferred rear-of-field position, and the going record on soft (sim-going 10/15, 0W3P) shows placing without winning.

runners_data.name: Copper Craft
runners_data.note: Has placed consistently over 8-12f at the Curragh and Naas on good-to-firm/good, but fades in finishes and soft-going form is extremely limited (1 run, unplaced); the natural rear-of-field style is compromised by redistribution into midfield in this shape, and a 0W0P record on comparable ground is a clear flag.

runners_data.name: Hosanna Power
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with no wins or places in 15 attempts at similar-going tracks — the form string of 000079 tells its own story; displaced into midfield here where it won't be comfortable, and W J Jack Cleary's 5lb claim is modest compensation for the lack of finishing punch this horse has consistently shown.

runners_data.name: Maker's Mark
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a consistent record of finishing 9th-11th in most outings, fades in finishes flagged, and just one run on anything resembling soft; Sadhbh Tormey's 7lb claim brings the weight down but this horse has shown no aptitude for finding extra when it matters across nine starts.

runners_data.name: Marians Gal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent placed form over 10f at the Curragh (2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th in recent starts), and today's trip on soft at Down Royal is closely aligned to that profile; sits naturally just off the pace in a race where that position is the sweet spot, making this one of the more straightforwardly placed runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Coul Dore
runners_data.note: Placed over 10f on good ground (2nd most recently) for the Crawford stable who have had a winner recently (T14: 1/2); soft-going experience is limited but the hold-up style and a fades-in-finish flag are complications — the recent placed form is the main reason this horse retains interest despite the style concern.

runners_data.name: Stonyfalls
runners_data.note: A three-year-old sprinter at heart — all five recent runs over 7f on good or soft, now being asked to step up to 1m2½f for the first time; a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield where it won't be fully comfortable, and the trip extension on soft ground is a major unknown that makes this a speculative inclusion.

runners_data.name: Swift Charm
runners_data.note: Has placed three times over 10f on good ground for Crawford, suggesting stamina to 10f is established; fades in finishes is the key flag and soft-going form shows three placed efforts in seven runs — likely to sit in midfield and stay on without quickening, making place rather than win expectations more realistic.

runners_data.name: Thistle Cross
runners_data.note: Four runs, all over 6-8f, all on good or standard — there is no soft-ground or 10f experience whatsoever in the form book; a hold-up type redistributed into midfield, carries a fades-in-finish warning, and the combination of trip extension, ground question and inexperience makes this a horse to leave out of strong assessments.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 10-12f including a 2nd over 12f at the Curragh on standard-to-slow; Robbie Colgan and Karl Thornton (T14: 2/4) represent a live yard, and genuine hold-up ability over this sort of trip gives this horse a realistic profile if it can find clear daylight through the large field in the straight.

runners_data.name: Talking Tough
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose best recent effort was a 6th over 14f on good — a thorough stayer at heart now asked over a sharp 10f on soft; fades in finishes, no wins or places in 15 similar-going attempts, and as a true hold-up horse displaced further forward than ideal, this is a very difficult profile to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Kilgharrahs Love
runners_data.note: Has placed over 10f on good ground (6th) and tried 12f without distinction; carries a headgear combination (tp) and has a 0W1P record in similar going across 15 attempts — a true hold-up type operating in midfield here, no jockey declared which is itself a note of caution, and the form makes it hard to construct a winning argument.

races.paceDynamic: Rising Sky is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field on soft ground at Down Royal, and with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead, this horse can dictate at a sustainable, controlled tempo from the front. The pace dynamic is essentially one-dimensional — Rising Sky will stride to the front, set a steady gallop over 1m2½f on testing soft turf, and is unlikely to be pressured into any kind of scorching early fractions. This creates a rail-hugging, compressed race shape where those tracking the leader through Cleopatra's Needle and Marians Gal occupy the most advantageous positions, while the bulk of the field will be queuing up in midfield unable to express their true running style. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear in a controlled-pace race — Stonyfalls, Thistle Cross, Folk Warrior, Hosanna Power, Kilgharrahs Love and others are genuine closers now mapped to midfield because the rear is oversubscribed, meaning none of them will truly be anchored at the back and late runs will be compromised. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can slot in behind Rising Sky without exertion, travel efficiently on soft ground, and produce a sustained rather than explosive finish are most advantaged by this shape.

scenarios.body: If Rising Sky sets a soft, uncontested pace and horses tracking closely from second or third sweep past in the straight.

scenarios.body: If Rising Sky's controlled soft-ground fractions prove slow enough that no challenger can close the gap in the home straight.

scenarios.body: If the pace collapses at the two-furlong pole and a handful of midfield runners find gaps to produce late surges.

scenarios.body: If the soft ground causes widespread stopping and the race degenerates into a slog with no runner able to finish cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Rising Sky's early fractions on soft ground will set the entire race shape — if Chris Hayes allows Cleopatra's Needle to creep dangerously close in the first half-mile, Rising Sky may be pressured sooner than expected and the prominent-stalker scenario unravels.

The 17-runner field on soft ground at Down Royal creates significant early jostling risk — watch for Marians Gal or Slaney Swagger getting shuffled back in the first two furlongs if the pace bunches, as both need to be prominent and may lose that position.

Stonyfalls and Thistle Cross are both stepping up considerably in trip for the first time on soft ground — either could capitulate turning for home and cause interference to horses trying to come from off the pace behind them.

Trainer W R Crawford has two runners (Coul Dore and Swift Charm) — watch for any market move on either as a yard double-entry in the same race sometimes signals stable confidence in one over the other, which could inform which is the intended runner.

Slaney Swagger returns after 192 days off for a trainer recording 3 wins from 4 in the last 14 days — watch the market carefully at the off as any strong support would suggest the yard believes the layoff has not blunted this horse's readiness.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Irish EBF Ulster Oaks Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Fiver Friday
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; Gavin Cromwell's six-year-old has winning form over 17f at Goodwood and a course win in softer conditions, making today's soft ground no concern, though the step up to 10f from recent outings is a slight query on the pace she will set.

runners_data.name: Apercu
runners_data.note: A O'Brien-trained six-year-old who has been consistently placed at 10f on good ground but soft form is limited; W J Lee takes the ride and she is well-placed to track the tempo if she gets a clean run from stall, though her OR-90 mark means she meets rivals on fair terms.

runners_data.name: Lady Lilac
runners_data.note: Sam Coen claims 5lb for Joseph G Murphy's four-year-old, who has been running at shorter trips on good ground; the step to 1m2½f in soft conditions is a stamina question worth asking, though she has placed at 8f on Heathrow ground before.

runners_data.name: Narlita
runners_data.note: Headgear: p; a natural front-runner whose prominent style cannot be accommodated in this shape given the surplus of pace — she will be squeezed back from her preferred position, and her best form at 8-10f on soft and heavy ground is genuinely relevant here, but racing against her natural instinct is a disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Beauparc
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted; Gerard Keane's six-year-old has winning form at 12f at Stavanger and Goodwood in staying company, and soft ground is not a problem at just 3/15, but her pace preference means she will likely be shuffled wider than ideal as the field jostles for position early.

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: Headgear: p; won at 10f on soft at Stavanger and on standard at Dundalk, so the conditions tick a box, but the Mrs John Harrington four-year-old ran poorly on her most recent soft outing and will find herself competing for a position she cannot naturally hold in this shape.

runners_data.name: Thrifty Of Digby
runners_data.note: Headgear: p; two wins from 15 starts on soft for the Harrington yard, and the most recent came at 10f on good ground in June — she is actually best on good to firm historically, and soft going here is a concern despite her natural pace, which she is unlikely to be able to express.

runners_data.name: Chica Guerrera
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's four-year-old has posted two wins and seven placings from 15 soft-ground starts, making her one of the most proven performers under today's conditions in the field; Ronan Whelan takes a confident booking and if she can settle just off the pace she has the soft-ground profile to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Chablis Rock
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie; Joseph Patrick O'Brien's three-year-old is lightly raced but won at 12f on good at Goodwood last time and placed at 10f on heavy at Hereford — the step to 1m2½f suits and her going record suggests she handles cut well; Declan McDonogh is a significant positive booking.

runners_data.name: Enchanted Lady
runners_data.note: The sole genuine hold-up horse in the race; three runs for A Oliver with limited form figures, and her only remotely relevant run was fifth at 10f on standard at Stavanger — soft ground is untested and this shape only favours her if the pace collapses dramatically, which is not the expected outcome.

runners_data.name: Stars Will Shine
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's three-year-old won over 7f on good and has placed over 8f, but this is a significant step to 1m2½f and soft ground; her soft-ground form over shorter trips last season is a positive but Chris Hayes will need her to be travelling kindly in mid-race to have any chance at this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner for Jack Foley who won at 7f on standard and has been running at 6-8f; redistributed to the rear of the map because the field is light on hold-up types, but she is emphatically not a hold-up horse — her chance depends on getting much closer to the pace than the map suggests, and the step to 1m2½f soft is a notable query.

races.paceDynamic: Fiver Friday is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Gary Carroll aboard, will stride into an uncontested lead from the outset on soft ground over 1m2½f at Down Royal. The field is heavily loaded with prominent-running types — Narlita, Beauparc, Diamond Exchange, Thrifty Of Digby, Chica Guerrera, and Liberation Date are all naturally pace-inclined but cannot all occupy those forward positions, meaning several will be forced to settle in unfamiliar territory behind the tempo. Fiver Friday will therefore set a measured, uncontested rhythm on soft ground, which historically at this trip rewards horses who can travel prominently and quicken off that pace rather than deep closers making up ground from the rear. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — of those, Fiver Friday is most assured of the lead, with Apercu, Lady Lilac, and Chablis Rock the likeliest to secure the next positions and settle into a genuine rhythm. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled, sustainable pace on soft ground at this distance strongly favours prominent racers who can track the tempo closely and produce a staying effort in the straight, not true hold-up horses finishing from off the pace.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapse in soft conditions is dramatic enough that Enchanted Lady or Liberation Date, both running from deeper positions, reel in a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapse in soft conditions is dramatic enough that Enchanted Lady or Liberation Date, both running from deeper positions, reel in a tiring leader.

watchPoints.text: Chablis Rock (Declan McDonogh) is the most dangerous individual in the race — lightly raced, going-adaptable, and a proven 12f winner who could be underestimated by the market against older handicappers.

Monitor how aggressively Narlita and Diamond Exchange push up from their enforced midfield positions in the first half-mile — if they inject pressure into the early stages the race shape could flip from Scenario A to Scenario C.

Fiver Friday's sectionals deserve scrutiny in the early stages; if Gary Carroll sets a truly soft pace on this going the race will compress entering the straight and strip the leader of her primary advantage.

Beauparc's tongue-tie is worth noting as a first-time or returned headgear signal — check markets for any support that might suggest connections expect it to sharpen her response in a race where her natural position is compromised.

Liberation Date's jockey booking — Orla Tynan (7lb claim) — and the horse's redistribution to the hold-up role means the claim is effectively cancelled out by the style mismatch; do not assume the weight allowance is a straightforward positive here.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Ulster Derby (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: New Zealand
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for A P O'Brien ridden by 5lb claimer Jack Cleary, which is notable over a trip and in a race where pace control is the key weapon; won over 7f at Goodwood but all recent form has been on quicker ground, making soft going a mild query, though the flat Down Royal circuit should not exaggerate that concern.

runners_data.name: Shosholoza
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien runner who has winning form on soft and placed in similar ground, making this ground profile his best to date; steps up sharply in trip but breeding and training angle suggest this 1m5f on soft is the intended target, and racing prominently off New Zealand's pace suits his pattern.

runners_data.name: Trojan Fighter
runners_data.note: Won over 1m5f on Good at the Curragh for P Twomey, so the trip is proven; wears a tongue-strap and has shown a tendency to travel well in a prominent position, but soft ground is untested in his recent form and four runs all coming on quicker surfaces is a genuine concern here.

runners_data.name: Harmani
runners_data.note: G M Lyons has placed this horse three times on soft or yielding including a win on good-to-soft, and the soft ground angle is one of his strongest credentials; by nature he wants to race up with the pace, but with the prominent positions already occupied by New Zealand, Shosholoza and Trojan Fighter he will likely find himself a position further back than ideal, which tempers the assessment.

runners_data.name: Huff'n'puff
runners_data.note: De Bromhead three-year-old who won over 1m on good ground 33 days ago and takes a significant step up in trip; his form is exclusively on quicker ground with all four runs coming on Good or Yielding, so the soft conditions are the key unknown, though he travels prominently which at least keeps him in the race shape.

runners_data.name: Mergus Serrator
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell runner with an uncertain style profile tagged U, giving no clear steer on where he will settle; three runs all on Good ground with no placing, and going into soft over an extended trip without an established pattern makes him difficult to assess with confidence.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Stars
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f at Leopardstown on Standard (AW) and placed at 1m4f on Good, so the trip is not an issue; races naturally up with the pace but the prominent tier is congested, meaning Chris Hayes may find him shuffled back from where D K Weld ideally wants him, costing him his most effective position.

runners_data.name: Madbadanddangerous
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's gelding won over 7f on soft and has placed four times from five runs across varying conditions, showing genuine versatility; rated a prominent type by nature but the crowded pace picture means Gavin Ryan is likely to find him in a hold-up position, which is not where his form is earned.

runners_data.name: Wyman
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's genuine hold-up horse who placed over 1m2f on soft 66 days ago, making this his first run in over two months; wears a tongue-strap and the step up to 1m5f on soft ground is a logical move for his style, with Nathan Crosse needing a strong late pace to develop if he is to get involved.

runners_data.name: Pierre Grosse
runners_data.note: Second trainer entry from Mrs Harrington, ridden by 5lb claimer Keithen Kennedy on a quick 15-day turnaround; all five runs are on Good ground and the style profile is uncertain, making soft ground on a step up in trip an accumulation of unknowns that is hard to resolve positively.

races.paceDynamic: New Zealand is the one confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for that position, he should be able to stride into a comfortable lead and control tempo on soft ground at Down Royal over 1m5f. Shosholoza, Trojan Fighter, and Huff'n'puff will press for prominent ground behind him, but none carries the pace aggression to seriously disrupt his rhythm, meaning the gallop is likely to be measured and sustainable rather than pressurised. This field carries more prominent-minded types than the race shape can accommodate — Harmani and Bay Of Stars are both natural front-rank horses who will be forced to race a position or two further back than ideal, diluting their effectiveness. The resulting race shape — a controlled, moderate-tempo lead over soft ground at a stamina-testing trip — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final quarter mile, rather than those trying to close from a genuinely rearward position.

watchPoints.text: New Zealand's lead is uncontested — watch whether Jack Cleary (5lb claimer) controls fractions correctly on soft ground, as any overly-generous early gallop could compromise the hold on this race shape entirely.

Harmani and Bay Of Stars are natural front-runners unable to secure their preferred position; watch the first two furlongs to see if either jockey pushes forward aggressively, as that could inject unexpected pace and destabilise New Zealand's rhythm.

Trojan Fighter's entire recent form profile is on Good or Yielding ground — if the soft ground query materialises in running, his prominent position early could leave him vulnerable in the final quarter mile of this 1m5f.

Wyman is the only structurally genuine hold-up horse in the field and has not run for 66 days; watch his energy levels early and whether the pace is strong enough to bring him into play in the final stages, which is the one scenario that could unlock a late closer.

races.paceDynamic: Grey Fable is the confirmed front-runner here, likely to bowl along from the front at a sustainable clip on soft ground over 1m5f, with Jurality, Deluca Chop, Folly Beach, and Just Another Eagle expected to press or track prominently. This creates a controlled, genuine pace rather than a false or sprint gallop — soft ground at Down Royal over this trip will ensure the tempo is honest enough to stretch the field out early. The prominent and midfield racers who can travel within striking distance of Grey Fable's rhythm are best positioned, as a lone confirmed front-runner setting a steady-but-real gallop on soft turf rarely produces a devastating finishing burst from far back. This shape materially favours horses who can race prominently or in early midfield and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — true hold-up closers face an uphill task. Note that the field contains significantly more hold-up types than the race map can naturally accommodate; Pebble Island, Numidia, Patrick Street, Calmafterthestorm, Plus Or Minus, and Idomything are all genuine hold-up horses remapped to midfield because they cannot all reach their preferred rear position, meaning those shown in midfield may not truly get there — Jurality and Deluca Chop are best placed to secure the prominent roles that matter most.

watchPoints.text: Grey Fable controls the entire tactical shape of this race — watch whether any prominent runner (Jurality, Deluca Chop) applies early pressure, as even minor harassment of the front-runner on soft ground could significantly change the tempo and alter which style benefits.|

Jurality ran just 13 days ago for the same trainer as Jazz Forever (Paul W Flynn) — watch for any stable jockey manoeuvre between the two runners, as W J Lee on Jurality versus Robert Whearty on Jazz Forever could signal which horse the yard is focused on.|

The bulk of redistributed hold-up horses (Pebble Island, Numidia, Patrick Street, Calmafterthestorm, Plus Or Minus, Idomything, Milverton) represent a cluster of horses unlikely to get their preferred position — watch early for crowding or traffic issues in the first half-mile as 17 runners sort themselves out on a soft surface.|
Folly Beach runs without a listed jockey — confirm the rider before race-off, as an unannounced booking or late change could signal stable confidence or the opposite in a wide-open handicap.|

Patrick Street is the most credentialed horse among the redistributed hold-up group (1 win, 3 places in last 5), having won at 12f on good at Goodwood — if it can get closer to the pace than its natural style suggests, it represents the hold-up horses' best chance of a placed effort.|

races.name: Event Co Marquees Maiden

runners_data.name: Counting Coup
runners_data.note: Lightly raced six-year-old with just one run on record (6th over 1m6f on good), so style and going response are genuinely unknown; any ability to settle and stay the 1m5f trip on soft will determine relevance.

runners_data.name: Daddy Long Legs
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained seven-year-old with a solid placed record at this sort of trip, including 2nd over 1m6f on good; has soft-going form (9th at 1m5f) and will likely settle prominently behind Steel Cut, making him a natural fit for the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: Double Indian
runners_data.note: Showed ability finishing 1st over 1m6f on similar going in a maiden context but has a noted tendency to fade in the finish; by nature a hold-up horse who has been pushed toward midfield because the field is congested with similar types at the rear — his winning chance depends on a stronger pace than Steel Cut alone is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Joe Cool
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer at lower OR (77) with wins on good and placed on soft; his natural instinct is to race prominently but, squeezed out of that position by the quantity of pace in this field, he is operating out of role and his chance must be discounted accordingly in a shape that does not give him a clear rail or prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Medadthebookie
runners_data.note: Long-absent (661 days since last run) four-year-old who has finished in the rear of maidens on good and heavy; hold-up style with a history of fading late, and the combination of absence and soft ground makes his engagement here largely exploratory.

runners_data.name: Murat
runners_data.note: Strong form profile for this race — three wins over 1m6f including on soft, placed in six of six starts on soft going; Peter Lawlor-trained seven-year-old who should slot in prominently behind Steel Cut and is arguably the best-placed horse in the field for the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Sea Celia's Star
runners_data.note: Beaten on debut at 1m6f on good (10th), hold-up style with a tendency to fade in the finish; Luke Comer runner who is 41 days fresh and has everything to prove on soft ground at this trip.

runners_data.name: Steel Cut
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with headgear, two runs at shorter trips (1m2f) — a 2nd on standard and 9th on good; stepping up significantly in trip to 1m5f on soft, and the key question is whether he stays the distance while setting the pace, but he will dictate the race shape regardless.

runners_data.name: Annacroft
runners_data.note: Debut runner for John McConnell, style and going preference entirely unknown; the absence of any form makes assessment impossible and connections should be noted as having a quiet recent record (0 wins from 27 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Duvessa
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien-trained four-year-old with a 2nd over 1m2f on good and an 8th on soft at shorter; steps up in trip here and the soft going form is a mild concern, though she is 40 days fresh and O'Brien's yard has strong recent strike rate (11/67 in 14 days).

races.paceDynamic: Steel Cut is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger pressing for the lead, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on soft ground over 1m5f at Down Royal. Murat and Daddy Long Legs are the most credible prominent horses and will likely settle just off Steel Cut, creating a measured but not truly pressured pace through the early stages. With the field containing more hold-up and prominent types than the track can naturally accommodate — Double Indian and Joe Cool are genuine prominent/hold-up horses pushed toward midfield in this shape — the race is likely to develop into a test of class and stamina in the straight rather than a tactical sprint. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently behind the leader or at least within striking range from the middle part of the field, with deep soft ground adding a premium on genuine stamina; pure hold-up horses are at a tactical disadvantage given the likely lack of a truly searching gallop to close into.

watchPoints.text: Steel Cut's stamina is the single biggest unknown in this race — he has only run at 1m2f and steps up to 1m5f on soft ground while leading; if he weakens entering the straight, the entire race shape collapses.

Double Indian and Joe Cool are both operating out of their natural positions in this field, creating potential mid-race crowding or shuffling as those two horses try to find their preferred racing position in the early-to-middle stages.
Murat's soft-going record is strong (placed in 6 of 6 on soft) but he has not run for 76 days — monitor market moves for any fitness concerns ahead of the off.

Medadthebookie returns after 661 days absent; connections should be watched closely in the parade ring for signs of fitness, as a lack of race-fitness could cause erratic behaviour in running and disrupt the pace of the race.

Annacroft is a complete unknown — a debut runner for a yard with zero winners from 27 runners in 14 days; worth monitoring if she drifts badly in the market, as that would confirm she is here for experience rather than as a live runner.
